why: GW's datasheet has the box (verify/.cache/waha/ds/ultramarines_Roboute-Guilliman.html: "SUPREME COMMANDER | If this model is in your army, it must be your WARLORD.", after the melee weapons and before CORE ABILITIES). The note quotes core 25.04 Fill Your Army Roster word for word (verify/.cache/waha/core.txt: "Some units have a rule on their datasheet stating that they must be your WARLORD. If you want to include one or more of these units in your army, you must select one of them to be your WARLORD."). It is the same note the approved Ghazghkull entries carry. Guilliman is the list's warlord, so the note is consistent with the list.

Wahapedia's Wardens of Ultramar prints "KEYWORDS – ALL MODELS: INFANTRY; EPIC HERO; EXPLOSIVES; IMPERIUM; TACTICUS / Dainal Komelius: PSYKER". Calgar's own sheet has no PSYKER, and the Bladeguard sheet has none either. kwOnly { Psyker:'Dainal Kornelius' } names the stats row and model line of that name (Wahapedia's "Komelius" is its misprint), and Psyker stays in kw. The kwNote no longer names Psyker. This is the same form as the approved Exalted Sorcerer and Scarab Occult entries (kwOnly Psyker, left out of the "come from" note), and it is the previous review's fix exactly.

The text is unchanged except that Wahapedia's three sub-headings (<span class="hi_custom">) are now bold lines (**Furor Tactics** …), as in verify/.cache/waha/ultramarines.html. Each Tactic gives "your unit's attacks" a weapon ability with no trigger. That makes it the approved any-attack label: your Shooting phase, the Fight phase, and the opponent's Movement phase for Fire Overwatch (core 15.08 WHEN: "End of your opponent's Movement phase"). Under 15.09, snap-shooting hits are never critical, so Furor and Malleus do nothing in Fire Overwatch. Purgatus's [PRECISION] does work there (24.28 needs no critical hit), so the rule as a whole rightly keeps Movement. DEATHWATCH ALLIES is mustering and adds no phase.
The Fight phase is either player's, so 'either', as for the approved always-on attack rules (Magna Imperator, Primarch of the XIII). The bold headings change nothing in the words that set the turn.

Movement is 'opp': the only attacks in that phase are Fire Overwatch, "End of your opponent's Movement phase" (core 15.08), where Purgatus's [PRECISION] applies. Shooting is 'your': the unit's own Shooting phase. These are the same turns as Primarch of the XIII and Magna Imperator, and the headings change nothing.

"Friendly **KILL TEAM** units with this ability" gives needs {all:['Kill Team']}. In this list only the Deathwatch Terminator Squad has Kill Team (Wahapedia KEYWORDS: INFANTRY; KILL TEAM; TERMINATOR; IMPERIUM), and it gets the rule. The heading change does not touch the subject sentence.

The labels match the now-bold headings exactly: from 'Furor Tactics' over "If the devastator doctrine is active for your unit, your unit’s attacks have [SUSTAINED HITS 1]", and from 'Malleus Tactics' over "If the tactical doctrine is active … [LETHAL HITS]". Each when quotes its condition. The names are also the new GRANTS and RULE_OPTIONS names (Furor, Malleus, Purgatus Tactics). kind 'all' is right because the text says "attacks". Purgatus is still left out because index.html passes the calculator no character allocation, so [PRECISION] changes no numbers (the approved convention). Two boxes rather than one pick is still right: Codex Adept and Author of the Codex can make several doctrines active at once.

data.js carries the todo's code byte for byte. 'own' is in HIDE unless opts.keep names it. The app calls resolveArmies(ARMIES, DATASHEETS, TABLE_ORDER) with no opts, so own never reaches a unit or row, from the datasheet or from the entry. No ARMIES entry stores own (tables.js skips it on entries), and the DATASHEETS rows carry the value as the plain stat (Deathwatch Terminator Sergeant W:'3', Impulsor InSv:'–', both GW's per the cached Wahapedia pages). The own block runs only for stats rows with from, and only under keep 'own' (tables.js --expand). It records the datasheet's value of each from-field that differs from the entry's value. Because ds is the uncopied datasheet row, nothing is mutated: row is a put() of a copy. sameLists strips own, so the tables gate compares only what the app sees, and it passes (141 entries, 18 lists). The app's resolved DW Terminator rows are W 4/4/3 with from Storm Shield on the two shield bearers, as before.
